faq.title: CBAHI, NCA, SAMA and PDPL - answered.
faq.a1: It is a Saudi-native compliance platform: a structured library of NCA / SAMA / PDPL / CBAHI / CCHI / NPHIES / SFDA controls, an evidence vault with bilingual OCR, six AI assistants that prepare and validate evidence, signed audit sessions, and one-click regulator export. The two demos on this page show both surfaces in your browser, with no signup.
faq.a2: Frameworks live in a global catalog. Your organization requests access (Org Admin or Super Admin can submit), a Super Admin reviews and approves, and the framework appears in your tenant. Audits can only be created against frameworks your org has been granted. Try the request flow in the framework demo.
faq.a3: 100% in AWS Middle East (me-central-2, Riyadh). Backups, embeddings, OCR and inference all run in-Kingdom. We do not call US/EU services for primary processing - relevant for SAMA Art. 6 and PDPL Art. 23.
faq.q4: Is the AI grounded, or does it hallucinate?
faq.a4: Every AI surface (validation, copilot chat, finding draft, summary report) is RAG-grounded in the actual framework text and your uploaded evidence. The copilot has a knowledge boundary: if it isn't in the framework or the evidence, it says so. Outputs include confidence scores and provenance metadata.
faq.q5: Does ArabAudit support CBAHI accreditation readiness?
faq.a5: Yes - the CBAHI program-specific packs (hospital, polyclinic, lab, primary care) are available as separate frameworks; chunked AI summaries are supported for the larger CBAHI editions. PDPL stacks alongside CBAHI for clinical data.
faq.a6: Each audit session runs against one framework, but the overlap engine maps a single uploaded document across NCA / SAMA / PDPL / CBAHI automatically - so the second and third audit sessions reuse evidence with one click.
faq.a7: When you finalize an audit session, ArabAudit computes a SHA-256 hash over all evidence, responses, and timestamps, then signs the manifest with your tenant key. Any subsequent edit to a locked session is detectable; the signed report PDF carries the hash for regulators to verify.

about.heroLede: ArabAudit is a Saudi-native Smart Audit Engine. We exist because audit tooling designed in Silicon Valley doesn't read Arabic evidence, doesn't understand NCA or SAMA, and doesn't care about sovereignty.
about.missionTitle: From audit panic to audit readiness.
about.missionP1: In 2024, compliance officers across Saudi Arabia were drowning in Excel chaos. Every regulator - NCA, SAMA, SDAIA, CBAHI - asked for the same evidence in different formats. Teams spent 12-week audit cycles copy-pasting between spreadsheets, Arabic documents OCRed badly, and reports took weeks to hand-write.
about.missionP2a: We built ArabAudit to end that. One upload satisfies three frameworks. AI maps 70% of evidence automatically. Bilingual findings and regulator-ready reports generate in minutes. And every byte stays in
about.y1b: Our founding team - a mix of CISOs, Big 4 auditors, and ML engineers - was running NCA ECC readiness assessments the old way: 38 Excel files, six vendors, zero cross-framework visibility. One client asked "can't an AI just do this?" We couldn't answer no.
about.y2b1: Riyadh-incorporated. We hired Arabic-native NLP engineers, negotiated SAMA and NCA framework access, and partnered with AWS me-central-2 for inference. Built the evidence ledger with SHA-256 anchoring before writing a single AI feature.
about.y2b2: The first paying customer — a mid-sized insurer — closed NCA ECC in 11 days instead of 10 weeks.
about.y3b: ArabAudit now runs audits for insurers, hospitals, banks, and Big 4 firms across KSA. 9 AI features live. Multi-framework overlap engine mapping NCA ↔ SAMA ↔ PDPL ↔ CBAHI automatically. We're just getting started.
about.v1b: Every byte of customer evidence, every embedding, every inference - stays inside me-central-2 (Riyadh). No US cloud primary processing. SAMA Art. 6 and PDPL Art. 23 compliance is a starting point, not a feature.
about.v2b: Every AI output is grounded in your evidence and the actual framework text. Confidence scores. Provenance links. If the AI doesn't know, it says so. The evidence ledger is tamper-evident by cryptographic design.
about.v3b: Not a translation layer. EN and AR are equal citizens: OCR, chat, findings, reports, and regulator exports work natively in both. Arabic documents aren't second-class inputs - they're first-class evidence.

pricing.q1: How does the framework add-on pricing work?
pricing.a1: Starter includes 1 core framework, Professional includes a multi-framework bundle. Need more? Additional frameworks are available at an annual fee per framework. Enterprise includes unlimited frameworks at no extra cost. Fill in the inquiry form and we'll send you a detailed breakdown.
pricing.q2: Why is pricing in SAR, not USD?
pricing.a2: Because we serve Saudi organizations exclusively. Billing in SAR avoids FX volatility, simplifies VAT and ZATCA compliance for your finance team, and matches how your budget is allocated. USD/EUR billing is available for Enterprise customers on request.
pricing.q3: What does Sovereign Gateway (on-prem) mean in Enterprise?
pricing.a3: Enterprise customers can deploy ArabAudit inside their own data center or private cloud - physical isolation of all audit data. Ideal for banks, defense, and government entities where even me-central-2 hosting isn't sufficient. Includes custom Active Directory and SIEM integrations.
pricing.q4: Can I audit multiple clients under one Professional plan?
pricing.a4: Professional supports one organization. If you're a Big 4 firm or audit partner serving multiple clients, Enterprise enables multi-tenant orgs - each client is isolated, with role-based access and separate evidence ledgers.
pricing.q5: What's the difference in AI Readiness between plans?
pricing.a5: Starter includes baseline AI Audit Readiness (coverage % per control, missing document detection). Professional and Enterprise include "richer readiness" - 90-day forecasting, domain-level narratives, cross-framework gap analysis, and predictive compliance scoring.
pricing.a6: Professional: 4-hour response SLA on all support tickets during business hours. Enterprise: 1-hour response SLA, 24/7/365, with direct access to your dedicated Customer Success Manager (CSM).
pricing.a7: All plans are annual billed. You can cancel at any point with 30 days' notice; all your audit data and evidence is exportable as a signed JSON archive regardless of plan. Enterprise contracts are typically 12–36 months with volume discounts.
pricing.a8: Yes. All invoices are ZATCA Phase 2-compliant, issued as signed XML + PDF with QR codes, and automatically submitted to the Fatoora portal. We are registered VAT payer under the Kingdom's tax regime.

pciDss.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
pciDss.tagline: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard version 4.0.1. A global security standard designed to protect cardholder data and reduce payment card fraud through technical and operational controls across six domains and twelve core requirements.
pciDss.summary: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard version 4.0.1. A global security standard designed to protect cardholder data and reduce payment card fraud through technical and operational controls across six domains and twelve core requirements.

d1.name: Build and Maintain a Secure Network and Systems
d1.desc: Establish and maintain network security controls (NSCs) and apply secure configurations to all system components to protect the cardholder data environment.

d2.name: Protect Account Data
d2.desc: Protect stored account data using strong controls and encrypt cardholder data during transmission over open, public networks to prevent unauthorized access.

d3.name: Maintain a Vulnerability Management Program
d3.desc: Protect all systems and networks from malicious software, and develop and maintain secure systems and software to prevent exploitation of vulnerabilities.

d4.name: Implement Strong Access Control Measures
d4.desc: Restrict access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know, uniquely identify all users with authentication, and restrict physical access to cardholder data.

d5.name: Regularly Monitor and Test Networks
d5.desc: Log and monitor all access to network resources and cardholder data, and regularly test security systems and processes to ensure the environment is protected.

d6.name: Maintain an Information Security Policy
d6.desc: An information security policy sets the direction for an entity's approach to managing information security across the enterprise and helps establish a culture of security within the organization.

cbahiClinic.name: CBAHI National Standards for Ambulatory Care Centers
cbahiClinic.authority: Central Board for Accreditation of Healthcare Institutions
cbahiClinic.tagline: CBAHI National Standards for Ambulatory Care Centers – First Edition 2019, Effective 1 January 2020. 11 chapters, 133 standards, 594 sub-standards (7 core).
cbahiClinic.summary: CBAHI National Standards for Ambulatory Care Centers – First Edition 2019, Effective 1 January 2020. 11 chapters, 133 standards, 594 sub-standards (7 core).

d1.name: LD - Leadership of the Organization
d1.desc: For any ambulatory care center, quality and patient safety depend on effective leadership. The leadership chapter addresses organizational structure, governance, roles and responsibilities of leaders, human resource management, patient and family rights, and quality improvement and patient safety.

d2.name: PC - Provision of Care
d2.desc: The provision of care chapter addresses the process of patient registration, patient assessment and reassessment, plan of care, consultations, patient's and family's education and participation in the treatment plan, cardiopulmonary resuscitation process, transfer and referral, and emergency care.

d3.name: LB - Laboratory Services
d3.desc: The assessment/reassessment of patients to determine the proper diagnosis, the course of treatment, and the evaluation of the treatment plan for future decisions may require laboratory services. To meet the patient's needs, the center should either provide basic laboratory services or outsource them to a recognized laboratory through a formal contracting process. This chapter addresses physical structure, staffing, safety program, specimen collection, equipment management program, labeling, quality management program, and point of care testing.

d4.name: RD - Radiology Services
d4.desc: The assessment/reassessment of patients to determine the proper diagnosis, course of treatment, and evaluation of the treatment plan for future decisions may require radiology services. To meet patient needs, the center should offer radiology services or outsource them through a formal agreement with a recognized radiology center. If the center provides radiology services, the services are expected to meet the necessary national guidelines on radiation safety. This chapter addresses staffing, radiation safety program, and equipment maintenance program.

d5.name: DN - Dental Services
d5.desc: Dental clinics pose a risk to patients that is different from the risks posed in other clinics in the center. This chapter addresses the peculiar dental standards that mitigate such risk, including staffing requirements, patients' assessment and treatment planning, patients' and families' education, medical records documentation requirements, and infection control requirements.

d6.name: MM - Medication Management
d6.desc: The standards in this chapter focus on medication management as it applies to outpatient prescriptions, and medication use in the day procedure unit, the emergency room, and owned outpatient pharmacies. The standards focus on scope of medication services, safe storage of medications, safe medication preparation, review of prescriptions for appropriateness, handling of expired medications, management of narcotics and psychotropic medications, and management of medication errors and adverse drug reactions.

d7.name: MOI - Management of Information
d7.desc: Information management is a cornerstone of patient care and the decision support process by center leaders. Center leaders are required to design and implement an information management plan that defines managing the information required by governmental and external agents, managing internal information requirements, maintaining the security and confidentiality of information, retaining records, and documenting and completing patients' unique medical record.

d8.name: IPC - Infection Prevention and Control
d8.desc: The ambulatory care center requires processes to support the prevention and control of infection that might be acquired or transmitted by patients, staff, and visitors while in the center. These processes reduce the risk or spread of infection and ensure that care is provided in a clean, sterile environment. To ensure staff and patient safety, infection prevention and control requires an effective center-wide infection prevention and control program that identifies, reduces, and eliminates infection risks.

d9.name: FMS - Facility Management and Safety
d9.desc: A safe, functional, and effective environment for patients, staff, and other individuals is crucial to prevent or minimize risks in the environment of care. The center leadership must provide all necessary support and resources to improve safety in the workplace in alignment with regulatory requirements. The center must maintain plans for managing the safety of the environment and must implement these plans. The center must collect and analyze data to determine the effectiveness of the plans and facilitate continuous quality improvement.

d10.name: DPU - Day Procedure Unit
d10.desc: Ambulatory care centers may have a day procedure unit where all day procedures are performed under local anesthesia, sedation analgesia, or general anesthesia. This chapter focuses on the standards required to safely manage patients in the day procedure unit, utilizing evidence-based criteria.

d11.name: DA - Dermatology & Aesthetics Medicine
d11.desc: Although dermatology and aesthetics medicine are recognized scopes of medical services that can be covered by the other chapters in this standards' manual, yet their wide spread practices in the ambulatory arena and their specific risky procedures warrants a separate chapter. The chapter, therefore, focuses on specific human resources and structural requirements as well as clinical risk management requirements.

demoAudit.aiGapDetected: AI detected a gap on CR-2.7.2
demoAudit.gapDetail: Privileged access monitoring insufficient - linked evidence shows 23% of infrastructure accounts lack session recording.
demoAudit.fdEnTitle: Privileged access monitoring gaps on infrastructure tier
demoAudit.fdEnDesc: Current PAM platform coverage is incomplete: 23% of privileged accounts across the infrastructure tier are not recording sessions. Access review logs show quarterly cycle is followed, but real-time monitoring and session capture are absent for these accounts.
demoAudit.fdEnRoot: Incomplete PAM license rollout; infrastructure tier deferred during Q2 2025 upgrade. No control-effectiveness verification after deployment.
demoAudit.fdEnImpact: Fails NCA ECC CR-2.7.2 mandatory session recording for privileged access. Potential regulatory finding on Q2 submission. Audit trail gaps could prevent forensic investigation of privileged-access incidents.
demoAudit.fdEnRec: Extend PAM coverage to all 23% uncovered infrastructure-tier accounts within 21 days. Deploy session recording, configure retention per NCA specifications, validate via 10 privileged-session tests, re-link evidence.
demoAudit.fdArTitle: ثغرات في مراقبة الوصول المتميز على طبقة البنية التحتية
demoAudit.fdArDesc: تغطية منصة PAM الحالية غير مكتملة: ٢٣٪ من الحسابات المتميزة عبر طبقة البنية التحتية لا تسجل الجلسات. سجلات مراجعة الوصول تظهر اتباع الدورة الفصلية، لكن المراقبة الفورية والتقاط الجلسات غائبة لهذه الحسابات.
demoAudit.fdArRoot: طرح غير مكتمل لتراخيص PAM؛ تأجيل طبقة البنية التحتية خلال تحديث الربع الثاني ٢٠٢٥. عدم التحقق من فعالية الضوابط بعد النشر.
demoAudit.fdArImpact: يفشل في الامتثال لضوابط NCA ECC CR-2.7.2 لتسجيل جلسات الوصول المتميز. احتمال وجود نتيجة تنظيمية في تقديم الربع الثاني. قد تمنع ثغرات مسار التدقيق التحقيق الجنائي في حوادث الوصول المتميز.
demoAudit.fdArRec: توسيع تغطية PAM لتشمل جميع حسابات البنية التحتية الـ ٢٣٪ غير المغطاة خلال ٢١ يوماً. نشر تسجيل الجلسات، تكوين الاحتفاظ وفقاً لمواصفات NCA، التحقق عبر ١٠ اختبارات جلسات متميزة، إعادة ربط الأدلة.

copilot.greeting: Salaam! I'm your audit copilot for Criterion CR-1.2.3. Ask me anything about your evidence, the control text, or NCA ECC requirements.
copilot.resp1: CR-1.2.3 requires the organization to establish, document, and approve a cybersecurity policy covering objectives, scope, and responsibilities. Based on your evidence (IT Security Policy v3.2.pdf), you satisfy the core requirement - but the annual review cycle is not explicitly documented in the policy header. Recommend adding a version control block.
copilot.resp2: نعم، السياسة الحالية (IT Security Policy v3.2.pdf) تغطي المتطلبات الأساسية بنسبة ٩٤٪ من ضوابط NCA ECC-2024. لكن النسخة العربية متأخرة بإصدار واحد عن الإنجليزية. يُوصى بمزامنة الإصدارات قبل تقديم التقرير للجهة التنظيمية.
copilot.resp3: Critical gap detected in CR-2.7.2 (Privileged Access Monitoring): 23% of privileged accounts lack session recording. Your PAM solution covers application tier but missing infrastructure tier. This fails the mandatory recording requirement. Recommended remediation: extend PAM coverage within 21 days.
copilot.resp4: Two linked documents: (1) IT Security Policy v3.2.pdf - approved signed Nov 15, 2025; (2) سياسة أمن المعلومات.pdf - approved Nov 22, 2025. Both carry CEO signature. Policy content matches 11 of 12 NCA requirements.
copilot.resp5: Drafting finding FND-2026-Q1-002: "Privileged access monitoring gaps in infrastructure tier." Severity: CRITICAL. Root cause: incomplete PAM deployment. Impact: fails CR-2.7.2 mandatory session recording. Recommended action: extend PAM coverage to infrastructure tier within 21 days.
copilot.fallbackEn: Based on NCA ECC-2024 control text and your linked evidence, this area is substantially compliant. Two minor gaps identified. Would you like me to draft a finding or show the specific clauses?

finding.lede: EN and AR finding drafts generated from evidence. Title, description, root cause, impact, recommendation - in both languages, every time.
finding.placeholder: Click "Generate finding draft" to see live AI generation...
finding.en_title: Insufficient automated incident response for Tier-1 security events
finding.en_desc: The current SIEM deployment lacks automated playbooks for Tier-1 incidents. Manual escalation averages 47 minutes, exceeding the required 15-minute threshold set by NCA ECC CR-2.4.3.
finding.en_root: Incomplete SOAR integration and absence of pre-built NCA-aligned automation playbooks. Current MTTD/MTTR metrics not monitored against baseline.
finding.en_impact: Risk of delayed breach containment; potential PDPL Article 38 non-compliance in breach scenarios requiring 72-hour regulator notification.
finding.en_rec: Deploy SOAR platform with pre-built NCA-aligned automation playbooks. Define MTTD/MTTR KPIs against 15-minute threshold. Timeline: 30 days.
finding.ar_title: استجابة غير كافية للحوادث الأمنية من المستوى الأول
finding.ar_desc: يفتقر نظام SIEM الحالي إلى أدلة التشغيل الآلية لحوادث المستوى الأول. يبلغ متوسط التصعيد اليدوي ٤٧ دقيقة، متجاوزاً الحد المطلوب وهو ١٥ دقيقة.
finding.ar_root: دمج غير مكتمل لمنصة SOAR وغياب أدلة التشغيل المعدة مسبقاً وفقاً لمعايير NCA.
finding.ar_impact: مخاطر تأخر احتواء الاختراقات. احتمالية عدم الامتثال للمادة ٣٨ من نظام حماية البيانات الشخصية.
finding.ar_rec: نشر منصة SOAR مع أدلة تشغيل معدة مسبقاً. تحديد مؤشرات الأداء الرئيسية MTTD/MTTR. الجدول الزمني: ٣٠ يوماً.
